title: CISO AI Security Provider Evidence Checklist
summary: A vendor-neutral record for testing AI-security claims against governance, architecture, controls, monitoring, and incident evidence.

sections.heading: Define the protected system and decision boundary
sections.content: Record the AI system, data, identities, tools, deployment context, and business process in scope before comparing providers. A broad AI-security claim is not evidence of coverage for a specific system.

sections.heading: Map controls to documented risks
sections.content: Require each proposed control to identify the risk it addresses, where it is enforced, what evidence it produces, and which residual risks remain.

sections.heading: Test operational evidence
sections.content: Evaluate integrations, deployment prerequisites, alert quality, failure behavior, administrator controls, and response workflows using the organization’s own representative scenarios.

sections.heading: Set monitoring and reassessment triggers
sections.content: Document changes that require reassessment, including new models, agents, tools, data sources, permissions, integrations, attack methods, incidents, and material changes in vendor architecture.

title: CEO AI Investment Governance Record
summary: A concise executive record for tying an AI investment to accountable ownership, measurable value, controlled risk, and a reviewable deployment decision.

sections.heading: State the decision and intended outcome
sections.content: Identify the business decision or workflow being changed, the accountable executive, expected outcome, affected stakeholders, and the evidence that will distinguish value from activity.

sections.heading: Record governance before deployment
sections.content: Assign ownership for business performance, data, technology, security, legal review, human oversight, and incident escalation before the system is placed into operational use.

sections.heading: Approve measurable release gates
sections.content: Define the minimum evidence needed to continue from experiment to pilot and from pilot to production.

sections.heading: Review realized value and exceptions
sections.content: Separate projected benefit from measured benefit. Review operating cost, adoption, quality, control exceptions, incidents, and unresolved risks on a dated cadence.

title: CHRO Workforce AI Governance Checklist
summary: An evidence checklist for AI used in hiring, workforce decisions, employee services, performance processes, and people analytics.

sections.heading: Inventory workforce decisions involving AI
sections.content: Record every material use case, the decision it informs, affected worker or candidate population, data used, vendor or internal owner, and whether a person can review or override the result.

sections.heading: Document data and evaluation evidence
sections.content: Identify training and operating data, population relevance, missing-data treatment, evaluation methods, known limitations, and evidence of performance across materially affected groups.

sections.heading: Define human review and recourse
sections.content: Specify who reviews consequential results, what information the reviewer receives, how an affected person can raise an error, and how corrections propagate through connected systems.

sections.heading: Monitor changes and outcomes
sections.content: Reassess when models, data, job families, geographies, decision thresholds, vendors, or workflows change. Track both operating performance and material workforce outcomes.

title: Board Cybersecurity Oversight Evidence Record
summary: A board-level evidence record for cybersecurity governance, risk visibility, material incidents, third-party exposure, and management accountability.

sections.heading: Define oversight responsibilities
sections.content: Record the committee or board responsibility, management owners, reporting cadence, escalation thresholds, and the relationship between cybersecurity and enterprise risk management.

sections.heading: Require comparable risk evidence
sections.content: Use a stable reporting structure that distinguishes exposure, control coverage, significant exceptions, incidents, remediation status, third-party dependencies, and accepted residual risk.

sections.heading: Prepare materiality and disclosure decisions
sections.content: Document who gathers incident facts, who assesses materiality, what financial and operational impacts are considered, who approves disclosures, and how unavailable information is followed up.

sections.heading: Test readiness, not presentation quality
sections.content: Request evidence from exercises, incident reviews, control testing, remediation validation, and material third-party scenarios. A polished dashboard is not a substitute for tested response capability.
